## Mapping Decisions

- One master record per source record, keyed by `RECORD_ID`; the nested `RECORD_TYPE` distinguishes PERSON and ORGANIZATION.
- Preserve the user's structured-address-first rule: for each source address, retain parsed parts when present and use `ADDR_FULL` only when parsed parts are absent.
- Preserve phone type only when a phone number is present.
- Map root `DATE` to `REGISTRATION_DATE` only for ORGANIZATION; keep year strings as provided.
- Keep relationship attributes in their existing nested source objects; no support table or join is needed.
- Do not normalize IDs, names, relationship values, or source qualifiers.

## Quality Notes

- The source quality score is 80.6. The mapper emitted 22 records; the verbatim checker passed and the routing report found no dropped source values.
- The analyzer reported one structural finding on record `2151`, which has two distinct address entries both labeled `REGISTERED`: a full-only India address and a structured US address. The bootcamper chose to preserve both entries unchanged; the finding remains documented and is not reported as a clean structural pass.
- The analyzer labels `TAX_ID_TYPE` custom/unrecognized. The current Entity Specification includes it; the release notes identify it as new in 4.4.0, while the saved SDK checkpoint records 4.3.2. Verify compatibility against the installed runtime and configuration before loading.
- The intentional PERSON/ORGANIZATION split prevents cross-type resolution. `EMPLOYER` uniqueness is 33.3%; `TAX_ID`, `NATIONAL_ID`, and `LEI_NUMBER` populations are sparse.
- Static checks do not establish matching semantics. Actual entity behavior remains unvalidated until a load and match-key review.
